title: INDEPENDENT Course STUDIES (Modules and Program)
markdown:
![](http://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/R-2-300x200.png)

**This is an exciting new learning format for learners to gain certified certificates as they choose one or more courses that are of interest to them as well as beneficial for their classroom or organization.  AGIs self-paced Independent Course Studies offer the ultimate in convenience for busy educators.  
  
These flexible self-lead- self-taught classes offer the learner graduate level college level training and the support materials from this site; and completing the associated assignments.****Independent Course Studies are a new format.  This format allows the learner to use Books and Journals as the focus of their research. Our certificates will be approved by American Canadian Board for Professional Training. Our school is accredited by American Council of and Development and QAHE.****To find courses, just visit the catalogue listing and send us the topic you want to study.**

**Each program has a no cost for the materials. Cost is only for the certificate for the completed courses for $49.95 for PDF certificate or delivery by mail for $79.95. Our instructors will evaluate your completed work and examination. All examinations must have an overall grade of 80 percent or Distinction.**

**Thank you for your interest.**

**American Group International**

**Email: americanecoleagadir@gmail.com**We offer these courses for short time study.

Book Learning/ Critical Review Grading Rubric

Essay. Please remember that it needs to be 12 Font. Times Roman. The essay should be about what you learned from the course. If you agree or disagree. It should be at least 1000 words, typed and double-spaced.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | **A 8-10** | **B 7-7.9** | **C 6-6.9** | **D 5-5.9** | **F <5** |
| **Summary (20%)**    How well does the student summarize the text? | Clearly presents author’s thesis and describes his/ her strategies for supporting it. | Presents author’s thesis and describes his/her strategies for supporting it. | Presents author’s thesis but may not provide sufficient description of strategies for supporting it. | Insufficient explanation of author’s thesis, and/or insufficient description of strategies for supporting thesis. | No explanation of author’s thesis, and/or no description of strategies for supporting thesis. |
|  | Clearly and succinctly describes organization and presentation of text. | Describes organization and presentation of text. | Describes organization and presentation of text, but may need more details | Insufficient description of text’s organization and presentation. | Poor or no description of text’s organization and presentation. |
| **Overall Quality of Analysis (20%)**    How well does the student analyze the text? | Exhibits clarity, complexity, perceptiveness, originality, and depth of thought about the topic. | Exhibits clarity, and some depth about the topic, but lacks the qualities of complexity, perceptiveness, and originality exhibited in level A. | Exhibits some clarity, though only minimal depth of thought about the topic. | Exhibit some faulty logic, and/or stereotypical or superficial thinking about the topic. | Exhibit little or no evidence of effective thinking about the topic (please note that there may be effective thinking in the composition, but not about the topic). |
|  | Provides excellent evaluation of text’s weaknesses or strengths; evaluative criteria are unique and interesting. | Provides clear evaluation of text’s weaknesses or strengths; evaluative criteria are unique and interesting. | Makes some attempt to present the weaknesses or strengths of the text; evaluative criteria are used. | Insufficient attempt to present the weaknesses or strengths of the text; evaluative criteria are unclear. | Poor to no attempt to present the weaknesses or strengths of the text; no obvious criteria for evaluation. |
|  | Uses creativity to interpret text (e.g., places it in interesting context or compares / contrasts with other relevant texts). | Puts text in meaningful context when interpreting it. | Places text in context. | Insufficient attempt to put text in context | Poor to no attempt to put text in context. |
| **Support of Analysis (20%)**    How well does the student select, summarize and/or paraphrase supporting evidence from the text to demonstrate and support analysis? | Exhibits command of focus, coherent organization, and interesting development (with carefully chosen, insightful details, examples, arguments, etc.) of the topic. | Exhibits control of focus, organization, and development (all of the subject matter is relevant to the topic but is not as insightfully selected as a response at level A) of the topic. | Exhibits some control of focus, organization (structure may be formulaic or be organized loosely around the topic), and development (may contain some poorly chosen information, but major ideas are adequately supported). | Exhibit insufficient control of focus, organization (way ramble, be repetitious, or locked into a formula), and/or development (it may be mostly descriptive or lack adequate support) of the topic. | Exhibit a basic/elementary sense of organization (may be purely descriptive or strictly formulaic), but ideas about the topic are generally undeveloped, illogical, irrelevant, or inconsistent. |

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Organization & Content (20%)** | Review is very well organized, containing an introduction, body paragraphs, and conclusion. | Review is well organized, containing an introduction, body paragraphs, and conclusion. | Review has separate introduction, body paragraphs, and conclusion, but connections among these could be improved. | Distinction between introduction, body paragraphs, and conclusion is unclear. | General structure of review is difficult to follow, and/or student failed to follow the prescribed format. |
|  | Paragraphs contain clear topic sentences, focus on a single issue, are coherent, and organized according to an obvious pattern of argument.    Effective use of transitional expressions and other signposts that make the structure of the document clear. | All paragraphs contain topic sentences, focus on a single issue and are coherently structured.        Some use of transitional expressions and other signposts that make the structure of the document clear. | Most paragraphs focus on a single topic and are coherently structured.          Topic sentences signal the structure of argument but may require more focus. Transitions are present and help connect parts of argument. | Paragraph structure needs improvement (some may be incomplete, or focus on too many issues, or be incoherent).      Topic sentences do not effectively signal structure of argument or lack focus / clarity.  More transitions are needed to develop argument. | Paragraphs are unfocused, incoherent or require restructuring.          Topic sentences are absent or unconnected to the paragraphs that follow.  Transitions are absent or used incorrectly. |
|  | Student’s tone and diction enhance the argument being made about the text under review. | Student’s tone and diction are appropriate for the argument being made about the text under review. | Student’s tone and diction are occasionally inappropriate for the target audience. | Student’s tone and diction are marginal.    Paper is much longer or shorter than the assignment requirement. | Student’s tone and diction are inappropriate.      Paper is unreasonably too long or too short. |
| **Grammar & Mechanics (20%)** | Clear, concise sentences. | Mostly clear, concise sentences. | Adequate sentence structure but may require editing for clarity/wordiness. | Poor sentence structure. Writing may be wordy or difficult to follow in places. | Very poor sentence structure, and/or uses inappropriate language or language that is too informal. |
|  | No grammatical errors.          Citations are included in the correct ACM format. | May have some minor grammatical errors.      Citations are included in the correct ACM format; may have minor errors. | Some grammatical errors, but these do not impede understanding.        Citations are included with some issues in ACM formatting. | Many grammatical errors.            Citations are included but not in the ACM format. | Significant grammatical errors, and/or  Contains errors that are identified by MS Word software but were not corrected.      Citations are missing. |

Please return your completed assignment to:

American Group International School of Agadir

Email as a PDF file with your name and date of birth and course of study to: [americanecoleagadir@gmail.com](mailto:americanecoleagadir@gmail.com)

All courses will be processed as quickly as possible. For mailing copies please included your exact name and address with the essay submission.
